1.w: The proverbs of Solomon: A wise child makes a father rejoice, but a foolish child is a grief to his mother.

2.w: Treasures gained by wickedness do not profit, but righteousness delivers from death.

3.w: The Lord satisfies the appetite of the righteous, but he thwarts the craving of the wicked.

4.w: The one who is lazy becomes poor, but the one who works diligently becomes wealthy.

5.w: The one who gathers crops in the summer is a wise son, but the one who sleeps during harvest is a shameful son.

6.w: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the speech of the wicked conceals violence.

7.w: The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the reputation of the wicked will rot.

8.w: The wise person accepts instructions, but the one who speaks foolishness will come to ruin.

9.w: The one who conducts himself in integrity will live securely, but the one who behaves perversely will be found out.

10.w: The one who winks his eye causes trouble, and the one who speaks foolishness will come to ruin.

11.w: The speech of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the speech of the wicked conceals violence.

12.w: Hatred stirs up dissension, but love covers all transgressions.

13.w: Wisdom is found in the words of the discerning person, but the one who lacks sense will be disciplined.

14.w: Those who are wise store up knowledge, but foolish speech leads to imminent destruction.

15.w: The wealth of a rich person is like a fortified city, but the poor are brought to ruin by their poverty.

16.w: The reward that the righteous receive is life; the recompense that the wicked receive is judgment.

17.w: The one who heeds instruction is on the way to life, but the one who rejects rebuke goes astray.

18.w: The one who conceals hatred utters lies, and the one who spreads slander is certainly a fool.

19.w: When words abound, transgression is inevitable, but the one who restrains his words is wise.

20.w: What the righteous say is like the best silver, but what the wicked think is of little value.

21.w: The teaching of the righteous feeds many, but fools die for lack of sense.

22.w: The blessing from the Lord makes a person rich, and he adds no sorrow to it.

23.w: Carrying out a wicked scheme is enjoyable to a fool, and so is wisdom for the one who has discernment.

24.w: What the wicked fears will come on him; what the righteous desire will be granted.

25.w: When the storm passes through, the wicked are swept away, but the righteous are an everlasting foundation.

26.w: Like vinegar to the teeth and like smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.

27.w: Fearing the Lord prolongs life, but the life span of the wicked will be shortened.

28.w: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectation of the wicked perishes.

29.w: The way of the Lord is like a stronghold for the upright, but it is destruction to evildoers.

30.w: The righteous will never be moved, but the wicked will not inhabit the land.

31.w: The speech of the righteous bears the fruit of wisdom, but the one who speaks perversion will be destroyed.

32.w: The lips of the righteous know what is pleasing, but the speech of the wicked is perverse.
